The DFF-feedback logic reduces to a clean counter:

- `inv0 = NAND(b0,b0) = ~b0`, so `b0` toggles every cycle.
- `xa,xb,xc,d1g` is the classic 4-NAND XOR, so `d1 = b1 XOR b0` (b1 toggles when b0=1).
- `na = ~(b0&b1)`, `and01 = ~na = b0&b1`; `ya,yb,yc,d2g` is again XOR, so `d2 = b2 XOR (b0&b1)` (b2 toggles when b0&b1=1).

Since outputs are recorded *before* the clock edge, cycle t records the current count, then updates. Starting at 000, the recorded value for cycle t is t mod 8:

- cycle0 record 000, update to 001
- cycle1 record 001, update to 010
- cycle2 record 010, update to 011
- cycle3 record 011, update to 100
- cycle4 record 100, update to 101
- cycle5 record 101, update to 110
- cycle6 record 110, update to 111
- cycle7 record 111, update to 000
- cycle8 record 000, update to 001
- cycle9 record 001, update to 010
